To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acoustic features and language based information are both useful for the recognition of emotions.

(a) the combination of acoustic and linguistic information leads to a significant improvement in speaker emotion recognition, (b) the combination of linguistic information and acoustic features can be achieved by a soft decision fusion using a neural net and (c) the combination of different classification methods can lead to a better performance than the combination of acoustic or linguistic information only.

the combination of acoustic and linguistic information is the most promising approach to a robust automatic emotion recognition and that the use of a hybrid SVM-belief network architecture for this task is superior to other approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a hybrid system for emotion recognition by acoustic and linguistic features.
a novel approach to speaker emotion recognition by acoustic and linguistic features.
the automatic recognition of a human speaker's emotion in spontaneous spoken utterances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach to the combination acoustic features and linguistic knowledge in a hybrid support-vector machine-belief network classifier yields a substantial gain in performance compared to the single approaches and the state of the art.
the integration of acoustic and linguistic information in speaker emotion recognition can be successfully achieved by the proposed architecture.
a hybrid architecture combining acoustic features and language based information in a soft decision approach provides a most robust and accurate automatic recognition of a person's emotion in speech.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of acoustic and linguistic information is a very promising approach to improve the recognition of speaker's emotions.

the integration of acoustic features and linguistic content for the recognition of a speaker’s emotion in the proposed soft decision fusion by a neural net is the most promising way to achieve a robust automatic emotion classification system.
the combination of acoustic and linguistic features for the recognition of emotions leads to a significant performance gain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of acoustic features and linguistic cues in the emotion recognition process can significantly increase the recognition performance.
the combination of acoustic and linguistic information is a promising approach to improve speaker emotion recognition.
the combination of both information sources can lead to a more accurate and more robust emotion recognition than the usage of each of these information sources alone.
